package diameter // import "github.com/skill215/diameterkit"

Package diameter provides bounded Diameter endpoints for public Go callers.

Nodes own peers, transport candidates, completion ports and resource budgets.
Explicit command policies bind application profiles, terminal destinations and
allowed answer sources independently of an adjacent DRA. Submit is asynchronous;
CompletionPort.Receive consumes the retained result and releases its charge.
Inbound.Respond validates an answer and restores the original arrival envelope.
Optional, finite in-memory duplicate caching supports multiple arrivals;
it provides no durable business or financial deduplication.

Dial/Maintain and Listener/Serve own transport admission and cancellation.
TCP/TLS adapters live in this module; Linux SCTP is in the separate
adapters/sctp module. Shutdown drains and uses DPR/DPA, Close terminates I/O,
and Wait joins cleanup. Completion ports must also be consumed or closed to
release resources.

Generated, owned codecs provide selected Base, Sh, S6c, SGd/Gdd and Ro/DCCA
profiles, plus explicit sms-fw compatibility bindings. They are bounded subsets,
not a declaration of complete protocol or target-OCS conformance. Sh-Data
helpers are explicit; codecs do not implicitly interpret business XML or SMS
payloads.

Legacy SCAP1 App0/271 needs SCAP1Accounting policies and strict local Vendor193
/ Acct19302 capabilities. PeerConfig.SCAP1Advertisement optionally selects the
reviewed old dual advertisement; standard Base validation remains the default.
SCAP1 remains SingleAttempt. Selected CCR bindings have separate, explicit Ro
recovery APIs; these do not authorize SCAP1 recovery or automatic financial
retry.

All production packages and dependencies are pure Go, targeting Go 1.26+.
The library has no persistence, subscriber lookup, charging ledger or
application restart orchestration. Current implementation boundaries are in
spec/progress.json.

	RoTransientRecoveryPolicy = "ro-transient-errors-v1"

type DuplicatePolicy struct {
	Class                                                            ClassID
	MaxProcessing, ReplayRetention                                   time.Duration
	MaxArrivals, MaxCanonicalBytes, MaxResultBytes, MaxEnvelopeBytes int
}

    is first admission + MaxProcessing + ReplayRetention and never refreshes
    on hits. MaxResultBytes counts encoded answer AVPs except Proxy-Info;
    MaxEnvelopeBytes counts encoded Proxy-Info only. Their sum plus 20 must fit
    MaxAnswerBytes.

type EndToEndSource interface{ NextEndToEnd() (uint32, error) }
    EndToEndSource supplies application E2E candidates only. It must be bounded,
    nonblocking and perform no I/O. A Node serializes calls outside its
    state gate; concurrent admission while the source is busy fails with
    ErrIdentifiers. Shared instances must be concurrency-safe across Nodes.
    No global uniqueness or persistence is supplied by this interface.

type Inbound struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Inbound owns one logical submission right and one original arrival. Message
    is the caller's independent mutable view; the private response envelope is
    never derived from that view. With DuplicatePolicy, one logical submission
    serves bounded arrivals and a volatile result cache; no business session is
    maintained.

func (in *Inbound) Check(ctx validation.Context) validation.Report
    Check freezes successful named evidence on the private request. It borrows
    the admitted workspace while running compiled pure rules outside the state
    lock. Failed checks leave the previous verdict intact. Frozen evidence
    cannot change.

func (in *Inbound) Done() <-chan struct{}

func (in *Inbound) Info() InboundInfo

func (in *Inbound) Message() pdu.Message

func (in *Inbound) Reject(ctx context.Context, failure ProtocolFailure) (ResponseResult, error)
    Reject uses the same preparation, validation and single commit gate as
    Respond. It accepts only named failures from the enabled policy; it cannot
    send success.

func (in *Inbound) Respond(ctx context.Context, body pdu.Body) (ResponseResult, error)
    Respond validates and bounds a complete answer before acquiring the one-time
    submission right. Failed validation or pre-commit ctx cancellation permits
    a retry. After Committed, ctx no longer cancels the write: return waits for
    its bounded primary write/close barrier. Committed is not peer/business
    success.

func (in *Inbound) Validation() validation.Report
    Validation returns owned evidence for the immutable received request.
    A committed response does not undo validation; expiry/close prevents further
    use.

type InboundInfo struct {
	RequestID         RequestID

type InboundPolicy struct {
	ApplicationBinding              ApplicationBinding // Independent of the adjacent peer and source allowlist.
	Command                         pdu.CommandKey
	Class                           ClassID
	Sources                         []pdu.Origin
	MaxRequestBytes, MaxAnswerBytes int
	ExecutionTimeout                time.Duration
	NoCache                         bool
	Duplicate                       DuplicatePolicy
	FailurePolicy                   FailurePolicy
}
    InboundPolicy explicitly enables bounded application request handling.
    Sources are terminal Origin identities, independently of the adjacent peer.
    Destination realm must be local; an absent host is allowed, a present
    host must be local. Select either NoCache (each arrival is delivered
    independently) or an explicit DuplicatePolicy. A zero/partial cache
    configuration never silently disables it.

type MaintainPolicy struct {
	InitialBackoff, MaxBackoff, Jitter, StablePeriod time.Duration
}

    MaxBackoff) plus [0,Jitter]. Only continuous Ready time resets failures.
    An all-zero policy disables Maintain, not manual Dial or Connect.

type Node struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}

func (n *Node) Accept(ctx context.Context, id PeerID, conn transport.Conn) (*Peer, error)
    Accept binds an already established transport to a configured peer. An
    opposite direction candidate may compete during handshake; open connections
    are never replaced.

func (n *Node) Cancel(id RequestID) error

func (n *Node) Close() error
    Close revokes all new work immediately. Wait is the I/O/borrower barrier;
    unconsumed completions retain their charge until Receive or Port.Close.

func (n *Node) Connect(ctx context.Context, id PeerID, conn transport.Conn) (*Peer, error)

func (n *Node) Dial(ctx context.Context, id PeerID, d transport.Dialer) (*Peer, error)
    Dial reserves an outbound candidate before invoking the dialer. Transport,
    TLS, CER/CEA and election share Timeouts.Handshake, clipped by ctx. Return
    means established, not necessarily Ready (a reconnection starts in REOPEN).

func (n *Node) IdentifierInfo() IdentifierInfo
    IdentifierInfo returns owned configuration and counters, never IDs or
    source.

func (n *Node) Maintain(ctx context.Context, id PeerID, d transport.Dialer) error
    Maintain runs one cancellable manager for an initially offline configured
    peer. The caller owns this goroutine. Cancellation closes its connection
    domain and waits for callbacks/I/O to return, but leaves the Peer reusable.
    Shutdown instead transfers existing connections to the drain/close
    lifecycle.

func (n *Node) NewCompletionPort(l CompletionLimits) (*CompletionPort, error)

func (n *Node) NewRoute(cfg RouteConfig) (*Route, error)
    NewRoute freezes ordered candidates and validates their command bindings.
    Multi-attempt modes require explicit same-terminal replay authority.

func (n *Node) NewSessionID() (string, error)
    NewSessionID creates an owned bounded ID. It does not create or track a
    session.

func (n *Node) Peer(id PeerID) (*Peer, bool)

func (n *Node) PrepareRoRecoveryRequest(ctx context.Context, body pdu.Body, opts RoRecoveryOptions) (RoRecoveryRequest, error)
    PrepareRoRecoveryRequest freezes a validated original request under
    Node/class scratch and identifier quotas. It performs no network I/O,
    allocates no RequestID, pending or completion, and never calls storage.
    ctx controls preparation only.

func (n *Node) RequestInfo(id RequestID) (RequestInfo, error)
    RequestInfo reports active Route requests only; it stores no completion
    history.

func (n *Node) Resources() ResourceSnapshot

func (n *Node) Retransmit(ctx context.Context, id RequestID, after AttemptID) (AttemptID, error)
    Retransmit admits at most one successor to after. Repeating a successful
    edge returns the same AttemptID while the request is active, even if ctx
    is canceled. Temporary absence of a ready connection or budget leaves the
    original deadline.

func (n *Node) RoRecoveryInfo() RoRecoveryInfo

func (n *Node) SchedulerInfo() SchedulerConfig
    SchedulerInfo returns expanded owned configuration, not queue contents or
    payloads.

func (n *Node) Serve(ctx context.Context, id PeerID, l transport.Listener) (result error)
    Serve owns l, including on admission failure. It serially accepts for
    one configured Peer, taking a passive candidate before Accept. Handshake
    failures close that candidate and retry after 100ms; Accept errors terminate
    Serve. Cancellation closes the listener and unfinished candidate, not
    established connections. Peer/Node Close or Shutdown own those connections.
    Return waits for all listener/handshake callbacks; Node/Peer.Wait include
    this borrower.

func (n *Node) Shutdown(ctx context.Context) error
    Shutdown uses one absolute deadline for all peers. Expiry may return before
    a delayed borrower exits; Wait remains the cleanup barrier, independent of
    Ports.

func (n *Node) SubmitRoRecovery(ctx context.Context, r RoRecoveryRequest, plan RoRecoveryPlan, p RoRecoveryProgress, port *CompletionPort) (RequestID, error)
    SubmitRoRecovery accepts a locally prepared original identity without
    invoking the identifier source. Frozen authorized targets and locally
    settled no-answer or explicitly enabled named error continuation are
    admitted. External records additionally require opt-in import checks.
    ctx controls admission only; accepted work uses its fixed deadline.

func (n *Node) Wait(ctx context.Context) error

	Capabilities LocalCapabilities

type Peer struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}

func (p *Peer) Close() error

func (p *Peer) Info() PeerInfo

func (p *Peer) Receive(ctx context.Context) (*Inbound, error)
    Receive waits across transport disconnection. Its ctx only cancels the wait.
    Explicit peer close stops delivery; Node.Close terminates all logical
    handles.

func (p *Peer) Request(ctx context.Context, body pdu.Body, opts RequestOptions) (Result, error)
    Request uses the same engine and a private single-completion port.
    Cancellation stops waiting only after the selected result and real writer
    evidence settle.

func (p *Peer) Shutdown(ctx context.Context) error
    Shutdown permanently stops new work in this peer's management domain.
    Its ctx bounds the whole drain/close operation; cancellation upgrades it to
    immediate close.

func (p *Peer) Submit(ctx context.Context, body pdu.Body, opts RequestOptions, port *CompletionPort) (RequestID, error)
    Submit uses ctx only for admission. A successful request lives until its
    configured deadline, Cancel, a terminal answer or connection termination.

func (p *Peer) Wait(ctx context.Context) error
    Wait waits for this peer's connection/manager/preparation borrowers,
    not application Inbounds or completion-port consumption. It does not close a
    Peer.

    chooses its business phase; the library does not run Tx or implement DDFH.

type RoRecoveryBinding struct {
	AllowedPeers                                []PeerID // Frozen for configured recovery targets; empty for the original Peer-policy fallback.
	ReplayDomain, EvidenceID, SessionEvidenceID string
	TargetID                                    string
	Retention                                   time.Duration

type RoRecoveryCheckpoint struct {
	RecordID                   [16]byte
	SegmentNo, ReservedThrough uint32
	Delivery                   DeliveryEvidence
	NextTrigger                RoRecoveryTrigger
	ReplayPending              bool
	ErrorResultCode            uint32 // Base namespace only, from a previously validated allowed answer.
	Unknown                    bool
}
    RoRecoveryCheckpoint is a finite application-owned observation,
    not authenticated history. For an uncertain crash, reserve the entire
    possibly admitted segment, set Unknown, and provide conservative
    Uncertain/MayHaveReachedPeer evidence.

type RoRecoveryImport struct {
	Checkpoint                                      RoRecoveryCheckpoint
	CheckedAt                                       time.Time
	SenderFenced, ProgressConfirmed, ClockConfirmed bool
}
    RoRecoveryImport declares application checks completed outside this library.
    No flag is proof of durable commit, fencing, trustworthy time or remote
    deduplication.

type RoRecoveryInfo struct {
	Stopped                     bool
	Limits                      RoRecoveryLimits
	Slots, Reserved, Held, Free int
	Classes                     []IdentifierClassUsage
}
    RoRecoveryInfo reports only owned bounded quota usage. No original request,
    record identifier, E2E, digest, historic answer or storage handle is

type RoRecoveryLimits struct {
	MaxRecordBytes, MaxTargets, MaxTotalAttempts, MaxSegments, MaxAttemptsPerSegment int
	MaxReplayAge, MaxResponseWait                                                    time.Duration
}
    RoRecoveryLimits bounds preparation and local recovery segments. Zero
    disables both. Deployment retention is a declaration, never proof of OCS
    deduplication.

type RoRecoveryOptions struct {
	SessionEvidenceID string // Application evidence for this frozen TERM session; no library session store.
	PolicyID          string
	Targets           []RoRecoveryTarget
	Limits            RoRecoveryLimits
	Validation        validation.Context
}

type RoRecoveryPath struct {
	TargetID string
	Peers    []PeerID
}
    RoRecoveryPath lists one terminal and its ordered alternate transport paths.
    Targets cannot repeat within a segment plan.

type RoRecoveryPlan struct {
	Import                 *RoRecoveryImport   // First external admission only; keep identical for an active duplicate.
	Alternates             []RoRecoveryPath    // Ordered, distinct frozen targets after the primary target.
	ErrorContinuation      RoErrorContinuation // Explicit policy for answers received by this segment.
	ErrorContinuationUntil time.Time           // Required only for SMSFWBeforeTx; after this instant only transient codes qualify.
	ResponseWait           time.Duration       // Zero disables Tr; positive values must fit the frozen record limit.
	TargetID               string
	Peers                  []PeerID
	MaxAttempts            int
	Deadline               time.Time
	Trigger                RoRecoveryTrigger
}
    RoRecoveryPlan is one finite, explicit segment. TargetID selects the first
    target; Alternates contains later authorized terminals. Peers are paths to

package diameter // import "github.com/skill215/diameterkit"

Package diameter provides bounded Diameter endpoints for public Go callers.

Nodes own peers, transport candidates, completion ports and resource budgets.
Explicit command policies bind application profiles, terminal destinations and
allowed answer sources independently of an adjacent DRA. Submit is asynchronous;
CompletionPort.Receive consumes the retained result and releases its charge.
Inbound.Respond validates an answer and restores the original arrival envelope.
Optional, finite in-memory duplicate caching supports multiple arrivals;
it provides no durable business or financial deduplication.

Dial/Maintain and Listener/Serve own transport admission and cancellation.
TCP/TLS adapters live in this module; Linux SCTP is in the separate
adapters/sctp module. Shutdown drains and uses DPR/DPA, Close terminates I/O,
and Wait joins cleanup. Completion ports must also be consumed or closed to
release resources.

Generated, owned codecs provide selected Base, Sh, S6c, SGd/Gdd and Ro/DCCA
profiles, plus explicit sms-fw compatibility bindings. They are bounded subsets,
not a declaration of complete protocol or target-OCS conformance. Sh-Data
helpers are explicit; codecs do not implicitly interpret business XML or SMS
payloads.

Legacy SCAP1 App0/271 needs SCAP1Accounting policies and strict local Vendor193
/ Acct19302 capabilities. PeerConfig.SCAP1Advertisement optionally selects the
reviewed old dual advertisement; standard Base validation remains the default.
SCAP1 remains SingleAttempt. Selected CCR bindings have separate, explicit Ro
recovery APIs; these do not authorize SCAP1 recovery or automatic financial
retry.

All production packages and dependencies are pure Go, targeting Go 1.26+.
The library has no persistence, subscriber lookup, charging ledger or
application restart orchestration. Current implementation boundaries are in
spec/progress.json.
